convoLines.text: "What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Here's the thing: Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Ming was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I braid grass while listening to plans. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Ming. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Sure — Still on your plan here."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Miriam has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Not that it matters."
"Ming is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said there was something you regretted. You didn't want to get into it. I won't ask. Just — are you carrying it any lighter?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Come here — Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Ming always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.' That's my read."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Miriam has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"I keep turning over the last thing Ming said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Ming's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening. Worth considering."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? I mean it."
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"Why do you ask? I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You saw it too, right? Hollow Belly. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Kudzu Root — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Nightlight — A soft green glow under the water. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"I show up. That's my part."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
You show them Kudzu Root — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Extremely normal, all of it."
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "Make of that what you will."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
"Take your time."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? But what do I know."
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "That night — I put down Big Loud at the treeline. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go before I say something sincere."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before? Just saying!"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "That night — I met The Static Kite at the treeline and barely walked away. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"I keep touching the spot where it grazed me. Like it'll explain itself."
"We lost the illusion that the treeline holds itself. That's a kind of progress."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I ran when I should have stayed. I think about it every day."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? I mean it."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Wheel of Teeth. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"We started on their secret, then got onto what's been happening."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you're angry."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

giftSample: Zenon watches you give the order. "Interesting. Nobody asked me."
"Got it," Zenon says flatly. "Orders are orders. Whoever gives them."
